'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**Four men who [[kidnap]]ped a businessman and his son in [[Herat]] are shot dead by [[Taliban]] police during a gunfight. The bodies of the kidnappers have been [[Public hanging|hanged in public]], in an apparent warning to others to not commit similar crimes. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-58691824 (BBC News)]
**A [[Military of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan|Taliban soldier]] is killed and seven more injured in [[Jalalabad]] when their convoy hits a [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]] planted by [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|ISIL-K]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/taliban-vs-iskp-in-nangarhar-s-jalalabad-one-killed-in-blast-101632581023513.html (Hindustan Times)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**A [[suicide attack|suicide]] [[car bomb]]ing near the [[Villa Somalia|presidential palace]] in [[Mogadishu]] kills eight people and injures seven others. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility for the attack, saying they targeted a convoy of cars traveling to the palace. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/suicide-car-bomb-somali-capital-kills-least-7-official-2021-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali]] recruits [[Russia]]'s [[private military company|PMC]] [[Wagner Group]] to fight [[Islamic terrorism]] in the country, according to a news outlet citing [[Russian foreign minister]] [[Sergey Lavrov]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mali-asked-private-russian-military-firm-help-against-insurgents-ifx-2021-09-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Panic buying]] of [[Motor fuel|fuel]] is reported at [[gas stations|petrol stations]] in the [[United Kingdom]] amidst a shortage of lorry drivers. A fuel purchase limit of [[pound sterling|£]]30 per customer is introduced at many locations due to "unprecedented" demand. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/sep/25/panic-buying-rather-than-shortages-causing-queues-at-uk-petrol-stations-aa-head-says (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Montana train derailment]]
**An [[Amtrak]] passenger train derails near [[Joplin, Montana]], U.S., killing at least three people and injuring at least 50 others. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/amtrak-train-derails-montana/ (CBS News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/25/us/amtrak-montana-train-derails.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] begins to require a [[Immunity passport#COVID-19|COVID-19 pass]] for people over the age of 13 years old as a precondition to enter hospitality venues and arts and cultural events. The [[COVID-19]] pass replaces most [[social distancing]] and [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask requirements]]. [https://nltimes.nl/2021/09/25/netherlands-now-requires-coronavirus-admission-passes-hospitality-events (NL Times)]
****[[List of Ministers of Economic Affairs of the Netherlands#List of State Secretaries for Economic Affairs|State Secretary for Economic Affairs and Climate Policy]] [[Mona Keijzer]] is dismissed from the [[Cabinet of the Netherlands|Cabinet]] by Prime Minister [[Mark Rutte]] after publicly criticising the cabinet's position on COVID-19 measures. [https://www.politico.eu/article/dutch-state-secretary-economic-affairs-mona-keijzer-fired-coronavirus-passport-criticism/ (''Politico'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Norway]]
****[[Norway]] lifts its [[social distancing]] rules and capacity limits on business, sport, and cultural venues, and other COVID-19-related restrictions, and also allows the reopening of nightclubs, as 67% of people have been fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in Norway|vaccinated]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/25/world/norway-ends-covid-restrictions.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports a record 847 new cases and one death from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-09-25/victoria-records-new-local-covid-cases-vaccine-progress/100491112 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[South Korea]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 3,273 new cases of COVID-19, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 298,402. [https://www.asahi.com/sp/ajw/articles/14447670 (''The Asahi Shimbun'')]
*[[Climate change]]
**[[Vanuatu]] launches a global campaign to seek an advisory opinion from the [[International Court of Justice]] (ICJ). Vanuatu bases its decision on being incapable with its own decisions to address rising sea levels and other challenges linked to climate change and wants the ICJ to establish responsibilities for climate change under international law. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/25/vanuatu-to-push-international-court-for-climate-change-opinion (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/452264/vanuatu-launches-campaign-to-take-climate-change-to-the-international-court-for-justice (RNZ)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[Kim Yo-jong]], sister of [[Supreme Leader (North Korean title)|Supreme Leader]] [[Kim Jong-un]], says that [[North Korea]] is open to holding [[Inter-Korean summits|another summit]] in [[South Korea]] if mutual respect between the two countries can be assured. [https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2021/09/103_315997.html?fl (''The Korea Times'')]
*[[Foreign relations of Afghanistan]]
**Russian foreign minister [[Sergei Lavrov]] says that the international recognition of the [[Taliban]] government "at present juncture is not on the table". The comments come after Taliban-appointed foreign minister [[Amir Khan Muttaqi]] appointed [[Suhail Shaheen]] as the representative of the Taliban to the [[United Nations]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russias-lavrov-says-taliban-recognition-not-table-2021-09-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Icelandic parliamentary election]]
**[[Icelanders]] head to the polls to elect the members of the [[Althing]], the oldest surviving [[parliament]] in the world. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/25/world/europe/icelanders-vote-in-volatile-election-with-climate-in-mind.html (''The New York Times'')]
**Early election results show that the [[First cabinet of Katrín Jakobsdóttir|three-party coalition]] led by [[Prime Minister of Iceland|Prime Minister]] [[Katrín Jakobsdóttir]] of the [[Left-Green Movement]] is expected to retain their majority. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/iceland-coalition-government-set-to-win-majority-but-future-uncertain-2553956 (AFP via NDTV)]
 
'''Sports'''
*[[2021 AFL Grand Final]]
**The [[Melbourne Demons]] win the 2021 AFL premiership against the [[Western Bulldogs]], winning 140–66. They also end their 57-year premiership drought, last winning the premiership in the [[1964 VFL Grand Final]]. [https://7news.com.au/sport/afl/melbourne-beat-bulldogs-in-afl-grand-final-c-4069244 (Seven News AFL)]
